newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-WALSH TO MISS 1997 COUNTY SEASON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WALSH TO MISS 1997 COUNTY SEASON.

text.p: West Indies captain Courtney Walsh confirmed on Thursday he would not be playing for Gloucestershire this year because of the extended Caribbean cricket season.

Test tours by India and World Cup champions Sri Lanka, as well as an extension of the regional first-class championship - the Red Stripe Cup - to 10 games from five, means the Caribbean programme will this year stretch into early June.

Walsh, who has played for Gloucestershire since 1984 and has been the team's captain since the middle of the 1993 season, said that even though he would not be playing county cricket he would still return to Gloucestershire in the summer "possibly to do a bit of coaching and for some charity games".
He left open the possibility of renewing his contract with the county in 1998.

The 34-year-old fast bowler is nursing a groin strain sustained in the fifth and final test of West Indies' recent tour of Australia, and could miss the first test against India at Sabina Park, Kingston, starting on March 6.
